cases.reason: The complete frozen gt-009 is recognizably decomposed across the browsing specification and design. The specification expressly covers home-bottom history display, retaining the latest ten and preservation after closing/reopening. Design decision 3 supplies Preferences (arkdata) and browse_history. These cover every element and applicable condition of this M01 object. The actual result asserts document coverage, not implementation or runtime success, and contains no unsupported additional finding.

assertionChecks.claim: The browsing specification covers home-bottom display of recently viewed products.
The specification covers the latest-ten limit, including what happens when the history exceeds ten.
The specification covers persistence after closing and reopening the application.
Design decision 3 covers Preferences (arkdata) storage and the browse_history key.
No element, condition or exception of the selected gt-009 is missing from the formal decomposition.

evidence.finding: M01:gt-009 requires home-bottom recent history, recent-ten retention, close/reopen persistence, Preferences storage and browse_history.
The original authoritative object agrees with the selected object; the original PRD independently supplies the same history and storage requirements.
Requirement and scenarios cover position, recorded products, latest-ten retention, the over-ten condition, and restart preservation.
The formally declared design completes the storage mechanism and key details.
M01 judges formal decomposition coverage. Runtime persistence proof is outside this proof question.
Both cited candidate documents belong to the declared formal corpus, rather than input-only basis or self-report roles.
